title: Introduction: Why this isn't a poker book
coreMove: Reconstruct the live decision before letting the final outcome judge it.
sourcePressure: The opening contract uses Pete Carroll's Super Bowl XLIX pass and the poker-versus-chess contrast to separate process quality from outcome quality under uncertainty, luck, and hidden information.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must not let the failed play become proof that Carroll was right or wrong; the point is that the public skipped the live-information question.

sourceAnchors.name: Pete Carroll
sourceAnchors.detail: His Super Bowl XLIX goal-line pass looked foolish after the interception, but the source uses it to show that outcome alone cannot judge the decision.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Pete Carroll's pass can sit on the table as the test: once you know the ball was intercepted, can you still ask what the call looked like before the throw?

sourceAnchors.name: Super Bowl XLIX goal-line pass
sourceAnchors.detail: The failed pass is the opening case for resulting, the habit of treating an ending as proof of decision quality.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The goal-line interception gives hindsight a loud final scene, which is exactly why the live decision has to be rebuilt separately.

sourceAnchors.name: poker versus chess
sourceAnchors.detail: Chess stands for near-complete visibility, while poker keeps hidden information and luck in view.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Chess flatters the fantasy of a complete board; poker keeps the hidden cards in the room.

counterintuition: Bad outcomes are secretly good decisions
tryThisNow: Think of one time luck affected you
Set a timer and reflect on a bad result

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital triage review after a missed sepsis warning
exampleSpecs.audience: clinical leads who run morbidity reviews
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a nurse is blamed for a call that looked different before the lab result came back
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Grace draws a vertical line on the review board, writes what was known before the lab result on the left, and refuses to let the later number cross the line until process quality has been judged.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A laminated triage flowchart curled at the corners under fluorescent light.

exampleSpecs.domain: architecture bid review after a lost museum contract
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the studio throws out a sound process because the museum chose a flashier rival
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Étienne lays the losing bid packet beside the original scoring sheet and separates the jury surprise from the criteria the team actually had.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The smell of plotter ink still hanging over the rolled museum drawings.

exampleSpecs.domain: charity gala rain plan after an outdoor dinner loses money
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether donors punish the planning team or inspect the weather odds and backup costs available before the storm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hannah rewrites the review agenda from final revenue to pre-event weather probabilities, vendor constraints, and the backup-tent quote they declined.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Hannah three weeks to stop seeing only the soaked table linens.

exampleSpecs.domain: youth soccer final after a goalkeeper pass is intercepted
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a child learns from process or from adult hindsight shame
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luca asks the sideline to describe the open defenders before naming the interception, forcing the adults to evaluate the pass before the ending.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Tell me what she could see before the kick," Luca says, holding the wet clipboard flat.
mustAvoid: copying the Super Bowl scene too closely

exampleSpecs.domain: university lab grant review after a rejected equipment proposal
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a junior scientist abandons a defensible grant strategy because one panel disliked it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marta covers the rejection score with a sticky note and first ranks the evidence quality, reviewer fit, and alternate proposals that existed when she submitted.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What can a rejection letter know that the submission day did not?

exampleSpecs.domain: tenant screening decision after a quiet applicant later damages an apartment
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a lawful screening process gets replaced by hindsight suspicion
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You place the signed checklist beside the repair invoice and mark which risk signals were actually visible before the lease was offered.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are looking at a repair invoice that seems to accuse last month’s checklist.

skillTargets: judge process without excusing sloppy process
recognize calibrated confidence in noisy outcomes

tryThisNowSpec: Take one recent win or loss and draw a before-after line. On the before side, list only facts available before the outcome; on the after side, list what the ending added.
